observable_outcome: internal/scheduler is imported by internal/application and nothing else; POST /v1/controls accepts an optional installation concurrency limit stored in a side table keyed by Control Intent revision with the seven existing ControlMode values unchanged; and GET /v1/queue/summary reports, from one bounded scheduler.Decide over the state read in the same transaction, the allocation (limit, its source, active, remaining), the waiting count broken down by the scheduler's own closed reason constants, and the exhaustion state naming which limit binds -- with a lowered limit proven never to invalidate a lease or claim that was already granted, and the L3 permit closure proven unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Scope boundary and dependency, stated before any code. Record that V2-030 is this task's dependency and must be complete: read internal/scheduler as V2-030 actually shipped it and record the exact names of its Decision type, its Plan.Decisions field and its closed reason constants. This task is wiring and observation only; it does not change any scheduler decision rule and does not edit internal/scheduler. The evidence must contain a table with one row per clause of cap-shared-resource-allocation's user_action (per-Requirement priority and its stated reason; per-Repository execution permission and concurrency limit; installation-wide and per-Repository concurrency limit; per-Provider availability and limit; current allocation, waiting reason and exhaustion) stating for each what this task makes observable and which task owns the remainder -- per-Provider is V2-028 with the surface in V2-067, multi-Repository is V2-030's local closure and V2-031's M7 gate. The evidence must state plainly that this task passes neither the M6 nor the M7 gate.

A2. Baseline, measured before changing anything. Record: that internal/scheduler is imported by no package outside itself (show the command and its empty result); that domain.PriorityAssessment's only references are inside internal/scheduler after V2-030; that GET /v1/queue/summary returns exactly requirements, by_requirement_status, increments, by_increment_status and active_executions; that no ControlMode sets a concurrency limit; and the top-level test names and counts of internal/scheduler, internal/application, internal/api, internal/store/memory and internal/store/firestore with all passing. Every pre-existing test must still pass at the end under its existing name with its existing assertions unchanged; report before and after top-level test counts per touched package.

A3. Import direction, asserted mechanically. internal/application imports internal/scheduler. internal/api does not, and must not: add an import scan over internal/api's own *.go files with go/parser that fails if any file imports internal/scheduler, verified first against a known-positive and a known-negative path and failing outright on a zero-file scan. Assert also that internal/scheduler's own import allowlist test from V2-030 still passes unchanged, which is what proves the edge could only point this way.

A4. The concurrency limit is a side table, not a mode. POST /v1/controls gains one additive optional object allocation_limit {installation_concurrent_executions}. domain.ControlMode keeps exactly its seven existing values: assert the value set is unchanged by enumerating it in a test. AllocationLimitRepository saves the limit keyed by Control Intent revision, at most once per revision, inside the same transaction as SaveControl, exactly as SaveControlRequestedBy does. Assert: (a) a control request with a limit stores the intent and the limit atomically; (b) a replay with the same request_id returns the same response and writes nothing further; (c) a replay with the same request_id and a different limit is an idempotency conflict; (d) a request without the field stores no limit row; (e) the revision the limit is keyed to is the revision the response reports.

A5. Limit validation. Accept 1..20 inclusive. Reject 0, negatives and values above 20 with 400, storing nothing and creating no Control Intent. Record why the upper bound is 20 by citing docs/architecture/validation.md section 5's concurrent Execution ceiling, and record why 0 is rejected rather than treated as a stop: a limit of zero would be a second way to halt the Loop that the control-verification pipeline does not observe, and pause-claim already exists for that with a proven verification path.

A6. Effective limit resolution. The effective limit is the limit attached to the greatest revision that declared one; a later revision that declares no limit does not clear it. Assert with at least four revisions in a fixture: limit at revision 2, no limit at revision 3, a different limit at revision 5, no limit at revision 6, and the effective limit is revision 5's. Assert that with no limit ever declared the ceiling is the section 5 design ceiling and ceiling_source says so, and that with a limit declared ceiling_source names the control revision. Resolution must be deterministic and clock-free.

A7. The L3 closure is unchanged, proven not assumed. internal/domain is not edited: assert by git diff that no file under internal/domain changes. Run internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go unchanged (it is a prohibited path) and record that its per-mode allowed-cell counts are still allow=8, pause-intake=1, pause-claim=2, graceful-stop=1, immediate-stop=0, emergency-stop=0, cancel=0, total 12 of 56. Assert the limit appears in no PermitRequest, no PermitDecision and no Effect by AST field-name scan over the new types plus a test that a permit decision is byte-identical with and without an allocation limit in force.

A8. Queue summary additions. QueueSummary gains allocation {limit, limit_source, control_revision, active, remaining}, waiting {total, by_reason} and exhaustion {exhausted, binding_limit in (none, installation-concurrency, runner-capacity)}. All five existing fields keep their names, types and meanings. Assert the summary is deterministic: the same stored state produces byte-identical JSON across repeated calls, with by_reason keys in a fixed order.

A9. The reported allocation is the scheduler's, and only the scheduler's. The summary calls scheduler.Decide and never scheduler.Apply: assert by AST scan that no non-test file in internal/application references Apply, and assert behaviourally that a GET /v1/queue/summary performs zero writes, stages zero outbox items and reserves no write quota (spy on the memory store's write paths and assert an exact count of zero). Assert the reported allocation count equals len(plan.Assignments) exactly, and assert the summary reports zero assignments when Decide returns none rather than reporting the active execution count as an allocation.

A10. Waiting reasons are V2-030's constants projected, and the projection is total. Add a table test that fails if any scheduler reason constant has no mapping to a reported value, and fails if any reported value has no scheduler constant behind it. Assert one scenario per reason constant, driving each rejection path through the summary and checking the reported by_reason bucket, and assert waiting.total equals the sum of the buckets and equals the number of considered candidates that were not assigned. Do not define a reason value this task invents.

A11. Exhaustion. Assert: (a) with the limit above the active count, exhausted is false and binding_limit is none; (b) with active equal to the effective limit, exhausted is true and binding_limit is installation-concurrency; (c) with the pool's own capacity binding first, binding_limit is runner-capacity; (d) exhaustion is computed from the snapshot's own capacity accounting and not by re-reading a candidate's reason value -- assert by constructing a case where a candidate's reason is resource-conflict while capacity remains, and checking exhausted stays false.

A12. A limit change never invalidates a granted claim. Build a fixture with active leases and claims above a newly-lowered limit and assert, in one test: every existing lease's id, increment id, execution id, fencing token, control revision, status, issued-at, expires-at and version are unchanged after the limit is lowered and after the summary is read; every existing claim is still present with the same resource, owner, repository id and mode (assert the claim multiset, not its length); no new assignment is planned; and the summary reports exhausted true with binding_limit installation-concurrency. Assert as the negative control that raising the limit again permits a new assignment on the next read without any repair step.

A13. Snapshot construction and its bounds. The Snapshot is built from RequirementsPage at the scheduler's own candidate bound, one synthetic Repository, one installation pool entry whose capacity is the effective limit and whose active count is the existing ActiveExecutions figure, and one Claim per active lease. Assert: (a) the candidate input is bounded and the bound is the scheduler's own, with a case at the bound and a case above it that fails closed rather than truncating silently; (b) no synthetic repository id, pool id or placeholder provider string appears anywhere in the marshalled response -- scan the response bytes for each placeholder literal as the positive control; (c) the read cost of one summary is bounded by a constant independent of Requirement count beyond the candidate bound, with the measured Firestore read count recorded at 10, 50 and 100 candidates as observations, never asserted as a threshold; (d) one summary read completes inside a context.WithTimeout of 30 seconds at 100 candidates, with the deadline as the assertion.

A14. The uniform-timestamp limitation is recorded, not hidden. Record the measured fact that domain.Requirement carries no capture timestamp, that every candidate therefore enters the Snapshot with a uniform zero CreatedAt, that the aging term is consequently uniform and the effective production ordering is the scheduler's documented ID tie-break, and that the starvation bound V2-030 proves in its own closure is therefore not yet observable in production. Do not manufacture a substitute timestamp from the clock or from an event scan. State the consequence in docs/operations/allocation-local.md in one plain sentence and escalate the missing durable field to the tech_lead as its own task.

A15. API and contract. Add the three new objects to the QueueSummary schema in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml with additionalProperties:false and all new fields in required, and add the allocation_limit object to ControlRequest. Assert 401 without authentication, 403 for the runner role and 200 for the owner on GET /v1/queue/summary, unchanged from today. Assert an unknown field in either request body is still rejected, and that every existing openapi-conformance assertion in internal/contracts and internal/release still passes.

A16. Owner console. internal/web/owner.html gains a numeric input for the installation concurrency limit on the control form and an Allocation section; owner.js sends the limit only when the field is non-empty and renders allocation, the waiting breakdown by reason and the exhaustion state legibly -- the reader must be able to see why work is waiting without parsing raw JSON. Add no external asset, script or font. Assert the control form still submits successfully with the field left empty.

A17. Documentation. Create docs/operations/allocation-local.md describing: that the limit is a side table keyed by Control Intent revision and explicitly not a ControlMode, with the EffectFromPermit reason why a new mode would stop the Loop; the effective-limit resolution rule and the 1..20 range with its source; that a lowered limit never revokes a granted claim and converges as work completes; the waiting reasons as the scheduler's own closed set; how exhaustion is computed; that the summary calls Decide and never Apply and makes no write; the single-repository, single-pool modelling and what is therefore not yet reported; and the uniform-timestamp limitation from A14. Do not edit docs/operations/scheduler-local.md (V2-030 owns it) or any other document.

A18. Determinism. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine in any new test; every wait is a bounded deadline poll over an injected clock and every timestamp comes from an injected clock. Run devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/application ./internal/api ./internal/scheduler three times in sequence and record that the verdict line and the output are identical each time, and run it once with -race.

A19. V2-067 convergence item. If V2-067 has landed, wire the provider registry's declared_ceiling to this task's effective-limit accessor and set ceiling_source accordingly, asserting the two surfaces report the same ceiling for the same state. If V2-067 has not landed, record that measured fact (show the command proving internal/application/provider_registry.go does not exist) and mark the item not applicable with its reason. Do not create the provider registry here.

A20. Measured notes for V2-045, recorded and not acted on. Record that this task adds an application -> scheduler import while ci/components.json declares application's dependencies as [domain] and scheduler's as [], so neither evidence key covers the other's public contracts; that internal/application already imports internal/quota whose roots belong to the infra component with no declared edge; and that this task moves the api, application, store-memory, store-firestore, web, contracts and docs component keys. Only the application and api records are issued here; name V2-045 as the owner of the remaining key movement under gate rule G6. Do not edit ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*; if a new component is genuinely required, stop and escalate to the tech_lead instead of editing.

A21. Evidence. Create .agents/v2/evidence/V2-068-application.json (id ev-v2-068-application, task_id V2-068, component application, correlation_id v2-068-scheduler-wiring) and .agents/v2/evidence/V2-068-api.json (id ev-v2-068-api, task_id V2-068, component api, same correlation_id), recording for every check the argv actually executed, the working directory, the timeout and a summary stating the measured result, with every acceptance item traceable to a named check. Record the execution environment identifier (uname -srm, go version, devbox environment). A skipped test is recorded with status skipped and is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). No prompt, no raw provider response and no credential value in any form may appear in either record. Register both with exactly two appended entries in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json whose evidence_hash is the sha256 of each artifact's final committed bytes; touch no other task's entry. devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts must be green with the records in place.

A22. Component evidence keys. The evidence_key recorded in each artifact is that component's key read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree where make check is green, with every touched file already git-added: a new file not in the index is invisible to that key.

A23. devbox run --pure -- make check is green, and it is re-run after the evidence commit so the secret scan reads committed history rather than an uncommitted tree. Record both runs and judge them by the verdict line, not by the shell exit status. No file outside allowed_paths changes.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push.
Never use git reset, git checkout --, git stash or git commit --amend.

V2-030 must be complete before this task starts. Do not edit internal/scheduler, do not add a scheduler decision rule, and do not rename or redefine any scheduler reason constant; if V2-030's shipped names differ from those cited in dp-v2-068, use the shipped names and record the difference.

Do not touch internal/domain. Do not add a ControlMode value, do not change controlSeverity, permitAllowed, Permit or EffectFromPermit, and do not add a field to domain.ControlIntent. The L3 closure the M1 gate proved must be provably unchanged, not merely unbroken by inspection.
internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go is a prohibited path: it must pass unchanged and its per-mode counts are re-measured, never edited.
Never let a limit change invalidate, revoke, expire or re-fence a lease or claim that was already granted. The limit is an input to the next allocation only.
Never report an allocation the scheduler did not decide. The reported allocation count must equal the scheduler's own plan, and the summary must never call Apply or perform any write.

Do not touch ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*; the component dependency DAG and the toolchain surface are V2-045's task. If a new component is required, escalate instead of editing.
Do not weaken any capability declaration in contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json; that file is not edited by this task.

Do not add a per-Provider or a per-Repository field to the queue summary: those halves belong to V2-028/V2-067 and V2-030/V2-031 respectively, and claiming them here would duplicate or re-open another task's scope.

Determinism is acceptance, not preference: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer, no goroutine in any new test. Waiting is bounded deadline polling over an injected clock, and a measured duration is logged as an observation, never asserted as a threshold.
A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record every skip explicitly with its status skipped and its reason, and record the execution environment identifier.
Never write a verification as passed that was not actually executed. If an acceptance item cannot be satisfied, stop and escalate to the tech_lead rather than fabricating or weakening it.
Every pre-existing test must keep passing under its existing name with its existing assertions unchanged. Report before and after top-level test counts per touched package.

Do not start a real Provider CLI (codex, claude or opencode) and do not touch any Google Cloud resource; Firestore assertions run against the emulator path the existing store tests already use, or are recorded as skipped with their reason.
Do not manufacture a Requirement capture timestamp. The uniform-timestamp limitation is recorded and escalated, never substituted.
